title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Corinthians chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Corinthians Chapter 6.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 6, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Dare any of you, having a matter against another, go to law before the unjust, and not before the saints?
But brother goeth to law with brother, and that before the unbelievers.
Now therefore there is utterly a fault among you, because ye go to law one with another.
If then ye have judgments of things pertaining to this life, set them to judge who are least esteemed in the church.
questions.correctAnswer: Dare any of you, having a matter against another, go to law before the unjust, and not before the saints?
questions.explanation: This is the first verse in the chapter, as stated in 1 Corinthians 6:1.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 6, who shall judge the world?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:2 states, 'Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world?'

questions.question: What are the saints deemed unworthy to judge, according to 1 Corinthians 6?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:2 mentions, 'are ye unworthy to judge the smallest matters?'

questions.question: What shall we judge, as mentioned in 1 Corinthians 6:3?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:3 states, 'Know ye not that we shall judge angels?'

questions.question: Who should judge if there are judgments of things pertaining to this life?
options: The least esteemed in the church
questions.correctAnswer: The least esteemed in the church
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:4 states to 'set them to judge who are least esteemed in the church.'

questions.question: What does Paul say to the Corinthians in 1 Corinthians 6:5?
options: There is no wise man among you
questions.correctAnswer: There is no wise man among you
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:5 states, 'Is it so, that there is not a wise man among you?'

questions.question: Who goes to law with brother, as mentioned in 1 Corinthians 6:6?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:6 mentions, 'But brother goeth to law with brother.'

questions.question: What does Paul identify as a fault among the Corinthians in 1 Corinthians 6:7?
options: Going to law one with another
questions.correctAnswer: Going to law one with another
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:7 states, 'there is utterly a fault among you, because ye go to law one with another.'

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 6:7, what does Paul suggest rather than going to law?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:7 says, 'Why do ye not rather take wrong?'

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 6:2, what will the saints do?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:2 states, 'Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world?'

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 6:3, what matters are mentioned as pertaining to this life?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:3 implies that if we judge angels, we should judge matters pertaining to this life, which includes the smallest matters.

questions.question: Is it stated in 1 Corinthians 6 that the saints will judge angels?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:3 clearly states, 'Know ye not that we shall judge angels?'

questions.question: Does 1 Corinthians 6:1 suggest going to law before the unjust?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:1 asks, 'Dare any of you, having a matter against another, go to law before the unjust?'

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 6, the saints will judge the smallest matters.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:2 indicates that the saints are unworthy to judge the smallest matters.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 6, Paul encourages the Corinthians to suffer wrong rather than go to law.
questions.explanation: While Paul asks why they do not suffer wrong, he is pointing out that they are not doing so, as stated in 1 Corinthians 6:7.

medium.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Corinthians Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who shall not inherit the kingdom of God according to 1 Corinthians 6:9?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:9 states that neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor abusers of themselves with mankind shall inherit the kingdom of God.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 6:11 promise will happen if someone is washed and justified?
options: They will inherit the kingdom of God
questions.correctAnswer: They will inherit the kingdom of God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:11 highlights that those who are washed, sanctified, and justified in the name of the Lord Jesus will not be counted among the unrighteous.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 6:10, who among these is mentioned as not inheriting the kingdom of God?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:10 lists revilers among those who shall not inherit the kingdom of God, alongside thieves and drunkards.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 6:8 suggest about the behavior of the brethren?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:8 states that they do wrong and defraud one another, indicating unethical behavior among the brethren.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 6:12, what is the relationship between lawfulness and expedience?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:12 affirms that while all things may be lawful, not all things are expedient, prompting consideration of the effects of one's actions.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 6:13 say about the purpose of the body?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:13 clarifies that the body is not for fornication but for the Lord, emphasizing its sacred purpose.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 6:14 indicate about God’s power?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:14 affirms that God raised up the Lord and will also raise up believers by His own power, showcasing His divine ability.

questions.question: What consequence is mentioned in 1 Corinthians 6:7 regarding disputes among brethren?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:7 highlights that it is a fault and shameful for brethren to go to law against one another.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 6:5, what does Paul say about wise men among them?
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 6:5, Paul expresses shame that there is not a wise man among them to judge between brethren.

questions.question: What should believers do instead of taking wrong according to 1 Corinthians 6:7?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:7 encourages believers to endure wrong and be defrauded rather than seek legal resolution against each other.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 6:3 imply about the saints' role?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:3 states that the saints will judge the world, indicating their authority and responsibility in spiritual matters.

questions.question: What is the main message of 1 Corinthians 6:9 regarding deception?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:9 warns believers not to be deceived about who will inherit the kingdom of God, emphasizing the seriousness of righteousness.

questions.question: Is it true that Paul advocates for legal disputes among believers in 1 Corinthians 6?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6 addresses the shame of believers taking legal disputes before unjust courts instead of resolving them within the church.

questions.question: Is it true that all things are lawful according to 1 Corinthians 6:12?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:12 states that all things are lawful, but not all are expedient, highlighting a distinction between legality and wisdom.

questions.question: Is it true that the body is for fornication according to 1 Corinthians 6:13?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:13 clarifies that the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord, emphasizing its sacred purpose.

hard.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Corinthians Chapter 6.

questions.question: What does Paul say about taking the members of Christ and joining them to a harlot?
questions.explanation: This is correct as it directly quotes 1 Corinthians 6:15 where Paul emphatically rejects the idea.

questions.question: What does it mean to be joined to the Lord according to Paul?
questions.explanation: This is correct as stated in 1 Corinthians 6:17, highlighting the spiritual union with the Lord.

questions.question: What does Paul instruct believers to do regarding fornication?
questions.explanation: This aligns with 1 Corinthians 6:18 where Paul commands to flee fornication, emphasizing its seriousness.

questions.question: What does Paul say about the body in relation to the Holy Ghost?
questions.explanation: This is stated in 1 Corinthians 6:19, where Paul emphasizes that the body is the temple of the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: Why does Paul say believers should glorify God in their bodies?
options: They are bought with a price
questions.correctAnswer: They are bought with a price
questions.explanation: This is found in 1 Corinthians 6:20, indicating the value and purpose of the body in glorifying God.

questions.question: According to Paul, what happens to those who commit fornication?
options: They sin against their own body
questions.correctAnswer: They sin against their own body
questions.explanation: This is explicitly mentioned in 1 Corinthians 6:18, stressing the personal impact of fornication.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'soma' in 1 Corinthians 6:19 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Soma' specifically means 'body' in Greek, as indicated in 1 Corinthians 6:19, emphasizing the physical aspect of the believers.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in 1 Corinthians 6:19 with the phrase 'temple of the Holy Ghost'?
questions.explanation: Paul uses a metaphor in 1 Corinthians 6:19 to express the idea that the body serves as a dwelling for the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to Paul's teaching on the unrighteous not inheriting the kingdom of God?
questions.explanation: Galatians 5:21 parallels the theme of unrighteous behavior preventing inheritance in God's kingdom, echoing 1 Corinthians 6:9-10.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage emphasizes the sanctification of believers similar to 1 Corinthians 6:11?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 10:10 speaks to the sanctification through the sacrifice of Jesus, resonating with 1 Corinthians 6:11.

questions.question: What comes before 1 Corinthians 6:19?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:18 directly precedes 1 Corinthians 6:19 and discusses the seriousness of fornication.

questions.question: What does Paul say about the lawfulness of things in 1 Corinthians 6:12?
questions.explanation: Paul states in 1 Corinthians 6:12 that all things may be lawful, but not all things are beneficial, indicating a balance in Christian freedom.

questions.question: What does Paul refer to as the body’s purpose in 1 Corinthians 6:13?
questions.explanation: In 1 Corinthians 6:13, Paul clarifies that the body is not for fornication but for the Lord, establishing its divine purpose.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Corinthians 6:11, believers were never involved in unrighteous acts.
questions.explanation: This is false as 1 Corinthians 6:11 indicates that some believers were previously unrighteous but have been washed and sanctified.

questions.question: True or False: Paul encourages believers to take each other to court rather than settle disputes among themselves.
questions.explanation: This is false; in 1 Corinthians 6:1-7, Paul criticizes believers for taking disputes to secular courts instead of resolving them within the church.

theological.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Corinthians Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 6:9 teach about human sin and its effect on salvation?
options: Certain sins disqualify individuals from inheriting the kingdom of God
All sins are equal and do not affect salvation
Salvation is unaffected by immoral behavior
Only unbelief prevents entrance into the kingdom of God
questions.correctAnswer: Certain sins disqualify individuals from inheriting the kingdom of God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:9 explicitly states that the unrighteous, including fornicators, idolaters, adulterers, and others, shall not inherit the kingdom of God, showing the seriousness of sin on salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification is taught in 1 Corinthians 6:11?
options: Believers are washed, sanctified, and justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of God
Sanctification is only a future event after death
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are washed, sanctified, and justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of God
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:11 affirms the doctrine that believers experience washing, sanctification, and justification through Christ and the Spirit, showing the transformative work of salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 6:12 teach about Christian freedom and self-control?
options: All things are lawful, but not all things are beneficial; believers should not be mastered by anything
Christians have unlimited freedom without restraint
Self-control is unnecessary since all is permitted
Lawful actions never require consideration of consequences
questions.correctAnswer: All things are lawful, but not all things are beneficial; believers should not be mastered by anything
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:12 teaches the balance of Christian liberty with responsibility, emphasizing that although many actions are allowed, believers must avoid being enslaved by any.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 6:14 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:14 shows God's sovereign power in raising the Lord Jesus and also raising believers by His own power, demonstrating divine sovereignty over life and resurrection.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified in 1 Corinthians 6:20 by the statement 'For ye are bought with a price'?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:20 highlights God's redemptive love as believers are bought with a price, signifying Christ's sacrificial love that redeems them.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 6:1-6 prepare for the biblical theme of the final judgment?
options: By affirming that saints will judge the world and angels, emphasizing their role in God's eschatological plan
By denying that believers have any role in judgment
By focusing only on earthly legal systems
By emphasizing the irrelevance of judgment for Christians
questions.correctAnswer: By affirming that saints will judge the world and angels, emphasizing their role in God's eschatological plan
questions.explanation: Verses 1-6 teach that saints will judge the world and angels, connecting to the eschatological theme of believers' participation in God's final judgment.

questions.question: In what way does 1 Corinthians 6:18-20 connect to the broader biblical narrative of the body as a temple?
options: It teaches that the believer's body is the temple of the Holy Spirit, echoing Old Testament holiness codes applied to new covenant life
It denies any spiritual significance to the body
It asserts that physical actions have no spiritual consequences
It replaces the concept of the temple with purely spiritual worship
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that the believer's body is the temple of the Holy Spirit, echoing Old Testament holiness codes applied to new covenant life
questions.explanation: Verses 18-20 link the believer's body to the temple of the Holy Spirit, affirming the continuity of holiness concepts from the Old Testament into the Christian life.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 6:15 and 6:16 teach about the believer's union with Christ and moral purity?
options: Believers' bodies are members of Christ and must not be united with sin, as sexual union symbolizes spiritual unity
Believers' bodies are irrelevant to their spiritual state
Union with Christ allows any behavior without consequence
Sexual union has no spiritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: Believers' bodies are members of Christ and must not be united with sin, as sexual union symbolizes spiritual unity
questions.explanation: Verses 15 and 16 teach that believers' bodies are members of Christ, so joining with a harlot is spiritually improper since sexual union signifies one flesh, underscoring moral purity.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 6:9 and 6:11 teach about the transformation of believers?
options: Those formerly unrighteous have been washed, sanctified, and justified, showing the power of salvation to transform lives
Believers remain as they were without change
Salvation does not affect moral status
questions.correctAnswer: Those formerly unrighteous have been washed, sanctified, and justified, showing the power of salvation to transform lives
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 11 together show that although some were unrighteous, they have been transformed through washing, sanctification, and justification in Christ.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 6:12 and 6:13 teach about Christian freedom and the purpose of the body?
options: Though all things are lawful, the body is not for fornication but for the Lord, emphasizing responsible freedom
Freedom means the body can be used for any purpose
The body has no spiritual significance
Self-indulgence is the core of Christian liberty
questions.correctAnswer: Though all things are lawful, the body is not for fornication but for the Lord, emphasizing responsible freedom
questions.explanation: Verses 12 and 13 together clarify that Christian freedom is not license for sin, especially sexual immorality, because the body belongs to the Lord.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 1 Corinthians 6:7-8 condones Christians suing one another to protect their rights. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It condemns believers suing fellow Christians before unbelievers as shameful and urges them to endure wrong rather than cause division
It encourages Christians to seek justice aggressively through lawsuits
It permits lawsuits only if they are righteous
It says nothing about disputes among believers
questions.correctAnswer: It condemns believers suing fellow Christians before unbelievers as shameful and urges them to endure wrong rather than cause division
questions.explanation: Verses 7-8 rebuke believers for lawsuits against one another before unbelievers, calling it shameful and urging them to rather be defrauded than create divisions.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 6:4 teach about church leadership and dispute resolution?
options: Disputes should be judged by those least esteemed in the church, indicating a role for church authority in resolving matters
All disputes should be taken to secular courts
Only the highest leaders should judge disputes
No disputes should be judged within the church
questions.correctAnswer: Disputes should be judged by those least esteemed in the church, indicating a role for church authority in resolving matters
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:4 instructs disputes to be settled by those least esteemed in the church, showing the principle of internal church judgment over secular courts.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in 1 Corinthians 6:17 by the phrase 'he that is joined unto the Lord is one spirit'?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:17 emphasizes the divine attribute of unity, showing the spiritual oneness between the believer and the Lord.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 6:19-20 connect to the theme of stewardship in Scripture?
options: Believers are stewards of their bodies as the temple of the Holy Spirit and must glorify God in body and spirit
The body is irrelevant to stewardship
Stewardship applies only to external ministry
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are stewards of their bodies as the temple of the Holy Spirit and must glorify God in body and spirit
questions.explanation: Verses 19-20 teach that believers' bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit, bought by God, and must be used to glorify Him, reflecting stewardship responsibility.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Corinthians 6:2 and 6:3 teach about the eschatological role of believers?
options: Believers will judge the world and angels, indicating their exalted role in God's final judgment
Believers have no role in future judgment
Only angels will judge the world
questions.correctAnswer: Believers will judge the world and angels, indicating their exalted role in God's final judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 2 and 3 teach that saints will judge the world and even angels, highlighting their participation in God's eschatological plan.
